producer_report.summary: Landing-intent and landing records are written by gh::land_pr through the athena-git RecordsWriter (remote-tip build, push with lease, bounded retry, local ref moved after push). For this send-back I strengthened the call-order test (criterion 4): it already checked that the bare remote holds the intent and no landing when PrHost::merge runs. It now also checks that the bare remote holds both the intent and the landing after land_pr returns. I did not rerun the full suite or the other tests after that edit. Only that one test and `cargo fmt --all` were run.

checks_run.note: ran before and after the edit

criteria_check.criterion: A free-function gh::land_pr test with a fake host reads the records branch and finds a landing-intent record then a landing record, in that order. Intent: PR number, head sha, head tree, expected base, job ids. Landing: PR number, head sha, host commit, merge method, commits with tree/job/verification, intent id. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria_check.evidence: gh.rs records_flow test, around lines 3640-3689, asserts record order and every intent and landing field. Written in the earlier round; not rerun this round.
